title: Relative global complete intersections descend along directed ring colimits
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(R_i)_{i\in I}$ a directed system of commutative rings with colimit $R$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $i_0\in I$, commutative $R_{i_0}$-algebras $B_0,C_0$, and a finitely presented $R_{i_0}$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $B_i=R_i\otimes_{R_{i_0}}B_0$ and $C_i=R_i\otimes_{R_{i_0}}C_0$ for $i\geq i_0$, and $B=R\otimes_{R_{i_0}}B_0$, $C=R\otimes_{R_{i_0}}C_0$; the induced maps are $1\otimes\varphi_0$. Suppose $B\to C$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection], meaning it admits a finite polynomial quotient presentation whose every nonzero residue-field fibre has dimension equal to the number of variables minus the number of equations. Then there exists $i\geq i_0$ such that for every $j\geq i$, $B_j\to C_j$ is a relative global complete intersection. No finite-presentation hypothesis on $R_{i_0}\to B_0$ or $R_{i_0}\to C_0$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0C33 (lemma-colimit-lci), relative-global-complete-intersection case, first proof paragraph; persistence at later stages by base change.

proof.text: Choose a witnessing presentation $T=B[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ and a $B$-algebra isomorphism $h:T\xrightarrow{\sim}C$. The presentation is a relative global complete intersection by the hypothesis and the definition; its structure map to $C$ is therefore the specified $1\otimes\varphi_0$, not an independently chosen ring map.

Apply Noetherian approximation to this presentation over $B$. It supplies a finite type $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra $P\subseteq B$, containing all coefficients, such that $Q=P[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $P$. The ring $P$ is finitely presented over $\mathbf Z$ by the finite-type/Noetherian finite-presentation lemma: $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian since any nonzero ideal is generated by its least positive element (Euclidean division), and the zero ideal is generated by $0$. The displayed presentation makes $Q$ finitely presented over $P$. Part (a) of the base-change lemma gives a $B$-algebra isomorphism $B\otimes_PQ\cong T$; compose it with $h$ to obtain $e:B\otimes_PQ\cong C$. Its restriction to $B$ is $1\otimes\varphi_0$ because both isomorphisms are $B$-linear.

source.place: Tag 0C33 (lemma-colimit-lci), first paragraph invoking Tag 00SU (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-Noetherian); Tag 00FP (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation); Tag 00SS (lemma-base-change-relative-global-complete-intersection), (1).

proof.text: Apply finite-presentation model-stage descent with $F(i)=R_i$, $A=R$, $A_0=R_{i_0}$, the original $B_0,C_0,\varphi_0$, and the $P,Q,e$ just constructed. Its hypotheses ask only that $\varphi_0$ be finitely presented, $P$ be finitely presented over $\mathbf Z$, and $Q$ be finitely presented over $P$; all have been verified. Obtain $i\ge i_0$, a map $P\to B_i$, and an isomorphism $e_i:B_i\otimes_PQ\xrightarrow{\sim}C_i$ whose composite with $B_i\to B_i\otimes_PQ$ is exactly $1\otimes\varphi_0$. Base change of the presentation of $Q$ along $P\to B_i$, followed by $e_i$, is thus a witnessing relative-global-complete-intersection presentation for the specified map $B_i\to C_i$.

source.place: Tag 0C33 (lemma-colimit-lci), first paragraph: factorization by Tag 00QO (lemma-characterize-finite-presentation), isomorphism descent by Tag 0C32 (lemma-colimit-isomorphism), assembled in the existing finite-presentation model-stage node; Tag 00SS (1).

proof.text: Fix any $j\ge i$. There is a $B_j$-algebra isomorphism $B_j\otimes_{B_i}C_i\cong C_j$: first identify its source with $R_j\otimes_{R_i}C_i$ by $(r\otimes b)\otimes z\mapsto r\otimes((1\otimes\varphi_0(b))z)$, with inverse $r\otimes z\mapsto(r\otimes1)\otimes z$; then use tensor cancellation $R_j\otimes_{R_i}(R_i\otimes_{R_{i_0}}C_0)\cong R_j\otimes_{R_{i_0}}C_0$. The formulas respect the balancing relations, and the composites are identities on pure tensors. On the structure map from $B_j$ the resulting map sends $r\otimes b$ to $r\otimes\varphi_0(b)$. Apply parts (a),(b) of base change to the presentation from step 3 along $B_i\to B_j$ and compose its presentation isomorphism with this one. It witnesses the required condition for $1\otimes\varphi_0:B_j\to C_j$. Since $j\ge i$ was arbitrary, the conclusion holds at every later stage.

source.place: Tag 0C33 (lemma-colimit-lci), end of first paragraph; persistence by Tag 00SS (lemma-base-change-relative-global-complete-intersection), (1); tensor cancellation as in Tags 00D2/00D0.

lean.statement: theorem exists_eventually_relativeGlobalCompleteIntersection {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (i₀ : I) (B₀ : Type w) (C₀ : Type x) [CommRing B₀] [CommRing C₀] [Algebra (F.obj i₀) B₀] [Algebra (F.obj i₀) C₀] (φ₀ : B₀ →ₐ[F.obj i₀] C₀) (hfp : φ₀.toRingHom.FinitePresentation) (hci : relativeGlobalCompleteIntersectionBaseChangeCondition (colimit.ι F i₀).hom φ₀) : ∃ (i : I) (hi : i₀ ≤ i), ∀ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j), relativeGlobalCompleteIntersectionBaseChangeCondition (F.map (homOfLE (hi.trans hij))).hom φ₀
lean.note: The auxiliary transparent definition installs only the canonical scalar action from the base ring homomorphism and applies the recorded ring-map predicate to 1 ⊗ φ₀. It is a scalar-action adapter for this statement, not an independent complete-intersection notion.
